title: How Things Move
objectives: I can use tiptoe, creep, glide, and dash to show how something moves.
I can use stumble and tumble to tell about a fall.
I can pick a movement word that says more than walk or run.
I can act out a movement word and tell about it.
rationale: Movement verbs show how an action happens, so a sentence says more than walk or run. These six are common in animal stories and adventures, and children can act each one out, which helps them keep the meaning. They are grouped by how the movement feels (quiet and slow, smooth and fast, and moves that go wrong). The unit revisits hunt, tiny, and describe, since an animal that hunts might creep or dash, and describing is the point of choosing the exact verb.

words.ex: Jo stumbled on a rock but did not fall.
words.ex2: I stumble when my shoelace comes untied.
words.nonExample: A runner who stays on her feet does not stumble.

apps.academic: Walk carefully so you do not stumble.

cloze.s: Watch your step, or you may ___ over that rock.

cloze2.s: The tired hiker began to ___ on the rough trail, but he did not fall.

words.def: To walk quietly on the tips of your toes.
words.ex: I tiptoe past my sleeping baby brother.
words.ex2: The cat tiptoed across the kitchen floor.

apps.academic: Tiptoe in the hall when other classes are working.
apps.writing: Use tiptoe to show how to move without a sound.

cloze.s: The baby was asleep, so we had to ___ down the hall.

cloze2.s: Zoe will ___ across the creaky floor so she does not wake the dog.

misuse.s: We tiptoed across the room by stomping as loud as we could.
misuse.why: To tiptoe is to walk quietly. Stomping is loud.

visual.alt: A foot standing on its toes beside a quiet face.

words.ex: The swan will glide across the pond.

apps.academic: Birds glide when they hold their wings still.
apps.writing: Use glide to show a smooth, easy move.

cloze.s: The eagle spread its wings and began to ___ across the sky.

cloze2.s: On the smooth ice, the skater can ___ without any effort.

misuse.s: The turtle glided across the sand in a hard, bumpy jump.
misuse.why: To glide is to move smoothly. A hard, bumpy jump is not a glide.

visual.alt: A swan floating along on a pond.

words.def: To run quickly for a short way.
words.ex: I will dash to the door and grab my coat.
words.ex2: The squirrel will dash up the tree when it sees the dog.

apps.academic: Do not dash in the hall; walk.
apps.writing: Use dash to show a quick run.

cloze.s: The rain began, so we had to ___ to the car.

cloze2.s: When the bell rang, the children ___ out to the playground.

misuse.s: The snail dashed across the garden faster than a race car.
misuse.why: To dash is to run quickly. A snail is very slow and cannot dash like a race car.

visual.alt: A child running fast with puffs of dust behind.

words.def: To move slowly and quietly, low to the ground.
words.ex: The cat will creep toward the bird.
words.ex2: Vines creep up the old stone wall.
words.nonExample: A race car does not creep; it zooms.

apps.academic: A caterpillar can creep along a branch.
apps.spoken: I creep so I do not wake anyone.
apps.writing: Use creep to show a slow, quiet move.

cloze.s: The cat began to ___ slowly toward the bird, keeping low.

cloze2.s: In the dark, we ___ down the stairs so no one would hear us.

misuse.s: The tiger crept down the road, racing as fast as it could.
misuse.why: To creep is to move slowly and quietly. Racing fast is the opposite.

visual.alt: A cat low to the ground looking at a bird.

words.def: To fall and roll over and over.
words.ex: The ball will tumble down the hill.
words.ex2: The puppies tumble over each other when they play.

apps.academic: Blocks tumble when you knock the tower.
apps.writing: Use tumble to show a fall with rolling.

cloze.s: When the tower of blocks is hit, the blocks ___ to the floor.

cloze2.s: The ball began to ___ down the steep hill, rolling over and over.

misuse.s: The boy tumbled up the hill in a straight line without rolling.
misuse.why: To tumble is to fall and roll. Going up in a straight line is not a tumble.

visual.alt: A child rolling down a grassy hill.

words.frame: The ___ began to tumble down the ___.

passage.title: The Cat and the Bird
paras: A little cat wants to catch a tiny bird. It tiptoes along the fence and creeps toward the tree. The bird sees the cat and dashes away. The cat tries to glide to the branch, but it stumbles and tumbles to the ground. The cat only licks its paw.

qs.q: What does the bird do when it sees the cat?
qs.why: The story says the bird sees the cat and dashes away.

qs.q: Why does the cat end up on the ground?
choices: It stumbles and loses its balance.
qs.why: The cat stumbles and then tumbles to the ground.

qs.q: What does the word tiptoes tell us about how the cat walks?
qs.why: Tiptoe means to walk quietly on the tips of the toes.

write.prompt: Draw an animal moving. Say or write how it moves. Use one new word.

study.task: Act out each word with your body. Which words move slowly and quietly? Which move fast? Which show a fall?

sentences: Say how you move when a baby is sleeping. Use tiptoe.
Write a sentence about an animal that can glide.
Tell about a time you had to dash.

given: The cat stayed low to the ground.
combine.model: The cat crept slowly along the ground.
Ben stumbled on a rock and almost fell.

discuss: Which movement word is your favorite? Why?
When do you have to tiptoe?
produce.explain: Explain how a cat moves when it hunts. Use the word creep.

constructed.prompt: Show two ways to move to the door: one quiet and one fast. Tell about each.
look: each word matches a real situation
constructed.model: I tiptoe to the door when the baby is sleeping. I dash to the door when the bell rings.

constructed.prompt: Tell about a child and a ball on a hill. Use stumble and tumble.
look: stumble is a trip and tumble is a roll
constructed.model: The child stumbled on the hill. The ball began to tumble down.

teacher.overview: Children learn six movement verbs, act each one out, and use them in a short story. The unit revisits hunt, tiny, and describe.

notes.va.stumble.v: Act out a small trip, then catch yourself. Stumble is almost falling; tumble is falling and rolling. Have children sort the two.
notes.va.tiptoe.v: Use a quiet game: tiptoe to the door. The word is also a compound of tip and toe; children can see both parts.
notes.va.glide.v: Have children glide a paper plane or slide their hand like a bird. Glide is smooth and easy, not fast.
notes.va.dash.v: Dash is short and quick. Use a short run in the gym with a clear stop. It is not the same as a long run.
notes.va.creep.v: Creep is slow, quiet, and low. The past form crept is irregular; say it aloud with a model sentence and do not drill the rule.
notes.va.tumble.v: Use a soft mat or a ball rolling down a ramp. Tumble includes rolling; link it to stumble as two kinds of fall.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'The mouse sees the cat. It wants to hide, so it does not walk. It dashes to its hole. The cat does not run; it creeps low and slowly. Then it stumbles on a stick, and it tumbles. Each verb tells me exactly how the animal moves.'
discuss: Which of these words would a hunter use?
How is gliding different from dashing?
misconceptions: Tiptoe means walking slowly in any way.
Stumble and tumble mean the same thing.
extend: Play 'Move Like It': call out a word and children act it out; add an animal each time.
Children draw a path with four stops and write a movement word for each stop.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit tiptoe and dash the next day as an opposite-feeling pair, again at one week, and use the verbs when children retell animal stories. They return as story language in unit 9.

frames: The ball began to tumble down the ___.
wida.oral: Partner A acts out one movement word without speaking. Partner B names the word and says a sentence with it.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (tropezar, caminar de puntillas, deslizarse, salir corriendo, avanzar despacio, caer rodando) are not reviewed by a native speaker; creep and dash have several possible Spanish verbs.
The past form crept appears in a cloze and is listed in family so the item resolves.
